description: Frozen Jacksonville 2013 exit-review player universe. This identifies continuity only; it does not control the 2014 roster.

players.identity: Changed-picture protection resets and on-schedule Stick/Drive timing were retained in spring. Tempo/substitution issues recurred; a full backup season gives role experience without enough game evidence for a broader ceiling.

A full season as QB1 now sits alongside repeated huddle/cadence/protection-point and two-minute evidence. Working hypothesis: an organized rhythm passer developing wider situational command; independent answers under disruption remain uneven or unobserved.

Assignment-sound spring work and cleaner final preseason operation supported QB3. No regular-season play is recorded. A narrower camp menu is a limit on observation, not proof that he can only run a small offense.
Cadence and feet improved; protection was correctly communicated on a retest. Timing became late when the presentation changed. His practice-squad season has no recorded individual evidence.

Track and protection communication survived changed pictures in spring/camp. His season includes varied receiving work and substantial lead-back experience; recorded fumbles locate distinct review questions, not an automatic decline diagnosis.

Track/check assignments held across spring looks; camp pickup-base correction held after teaching. The Week 15 fumble remains a cause question. Neither reserve status nor a productive run settles his full range.
Spring/preseason route assignments and backfield work provide useful positive evidence; the season gives RB2 experience. Protection and particular run/fumble causes still need individual review.

Fullback responsibilities and receiving appearances show the jobs he encountered; individual lead-block/protection execution is poorly documented. A lack of fumbles or a successful catch does not certify the whole role.
Preseason Miami and Atlanta records describe assignment-correct route work. There is no documented practice-squad-season assessment, so an all-around back judgment would outrun the evidence.
No individual spring, preseason or practice-squad rep is recorded. The staff owes an honest evaluation; absence of a record establishes neither a physical shortfall nor a low ceiling.

Alignment, assignment and cross-unit communication were supported in spring; recorded corrections were taken. His season brought movable receiver jobs, then an unexplained parked evaluation. One postseason fumble is a rep to understand.

Landmarks, alignment and formation communication held across spring/camp. A full season as the primary receiver gives a broad shared-QB sample; target outcomes do not by themselves establish route fault.

Cumulative camp operation placed him in the leading pair; alignment/motion correction closure remains unrecorded. The later-season Z workload adds experience but cannot establish every route or blocking capability.

He transferred into the WR3 job with the concept structure intact. Individual practice detail is thin; the Week 4 fumble and target outcomes need context. Old randomly allocated return credits do not assess him.

San Diego supplies representative receiving opportunities, including Split Leak; practice assessment is thin. Week 11 inactivity followed roster composition changes and is not recorded as a finding against his play.
No individual 2013 rep or practice-squad evaluation is recorded. He asked for written feedback; the missing communication belongs to the staff before any conclusion about his football ability.

Formation communication, dependable all-around camp operation and assignment-correct preseason routes are supported. Extensive protection assignments make low receiving totals an incomplete picture; in-line execution still needs his own review.
Camp/preseason assignment reliability and route work provide a baseline. TE3 usage leaves individual blocking and broader receiving capability underobserved, not disproven.

Attached/flex alignment and route movement transferred across spring, preseason and the assigned season role. Base/hand work in attached blocking required repeated teaching; assignment understanding and physical execution must stay separate.

A full season of tackle responsibility supplies experience and review material. The individual record supports some correctly identified work with physical-leverage questions, not a complete grade from sacks charged by the old engine.

Point echoes, changed-front communication and twist exchanges were retained through spring/camp. The rookie then started a full season. Physical answers to power/inside counters remain a question, distinct from understanding.

Identification and interior communication have supporting camp evidence; isolated recovery after losing leverage was less settled. Missing weeks caused by the injury-record problem are not an effort or learning finding.
Communication and point/echo/confirm work provide a recorded veteran contribution. His two starts and reserve period deserve the promised review. Entry 79 retirement ends training eligibility.

Correct identification with physical-leverage loss and recovery appears in preseason. Swing/six-lineman usage provides experience; it does not certify every tackle job or explain every team run result.

He took over the center role during the season and the recorded operation held. Individual season grades were not returned; the protection unit's outcomes cannot establish all of his physical execution.

Correct identification and recovery appear in preseason; shared interior exchange work improved in spring. Individual leverage and the Week 2 sack cause remain underclassified. A VERIFY retirement row does not retire him.

Combination calls were consistent late in camp and supported the starting decision. Physical recovery/leverage was less settled. Injury-limited opportunity cannot be interpreted as toughness, effort or stalled learning.
The individual record is too thin to establish technique strengths or faults; charged sacks do not prove he even participated. The reserve-order change cited Pasztor's work, not an Asper failure.
Camp identified a stable interior run combination with Miller. His season contains different rush/contain purposes; sack and pressure counts cannot tell whether he followed those purposes.
Camp established edge/strong-side rotation experience; the player reported that paired teaching helped. Individual season rush/run execution is not yet fully classified.
Recorded camp edge/strong-side work provides limited baseline evidence. A prolonged absence left individual evaluation thin; historical medical gaps are not ability conclusions.
Camp identified leading edge pressure. The season requires separating called containment from chances to finish; raw sack totals cannot provide that split.
The role history includes an edge rotation, but no sufficient individual spring/camp evaluation identifies why he ranked there. It is not a complete description of his capacity.
Base-front fit was supported in camp, including the interior pairing with Marks. A run-first assignment can suppress rush opportunities; individual game evidence still needs classification.
Experience across front jobs is recorded, but the individual physical/technical evaluation is thin. A stronger camp pairing elsewhere does not identify his defect or settle his best job.
Camp/preseason rush finishes earned rotational work. The season does not record his rush opportunity denominator, so low production cannot distinguish limited opportunity from execution.
Rookie minicamp recorded known edge/contain assignments and an immediate rush-lane correction. Later individual evidence is thin despite dressing late in the year.
His long early absence was prolonged by the club's record failure. Later interior rotation supplies review material, but there is no sound individual ability conclusion from counts alone.
Seven dressed games have no individual written evaluation; later inactivity was a game-day-list choice. Neither physical shortfall nor effort failure is established.
No individual 2013 rep or practice-squad evaluation is recorded. His question about weight does not establish that weight is the problem.
Prior NFL experience is recorded, but this staff's 2013 individual evidence is missing. A vacant roster place does not establish why he was not promoted.

Dated branch records support communication when Posluszny was absent, including the reshaped late-season base. Tight-end targets and run outcomes require assignment/help review before individual judgment.

A season of fits/calls and an explicit request to clarify shared command belong in his profile. Much in-season evidence is unit-level; the independent medical hold limits current work, not his standing as a learner.
Branch records describe ready operation beside Smith during teammate absences and retained narrow coverage/communication work. His full individual fit/coverage review remains owed.
Spring coverage correction held under changed looks, with useful movement/pursuit evidence. Camp fit overruns recurred after an earlier correction, narrowing the assigned job at that time.
Late-season base-reserve responsibility provides meaningful exposure but no completed fit-by-fit assessment. Tackles locate involvement rather than prove the fit was right.
Camp supports sound leverage and clear exchanges. The full season raises meaningful help/target questions, but totals cannot reconstruct individual responsibility.
He won and held the outside job on camp evidence; pair-level coverage reads and teams portability add context. No specific individual technique fault is recorded, and injury is not effort evidence.

Basic alignment/coverage and spring correction retention are supported; controlled pursuit-angle work improved. His rookie starting experience broadens the questions, not proof of complete live tackling or help mastery.
Camp identified stabilizing safety communication. His request for clear help priorities exposes a shared-rule question, not proof of a coverage defect or an elite grade from interceptions.

Communication, leverage and self-correction were retained across rookie camp, OTAs and camp, including inside/outside presentations. Nickel experience is real; recovery after lost leverage and the parked outside evaluation remain unresolved.

He stepped into outside work after Ball's injury. Help directives changed around him, while the record lacks an individual technique finding. That experience is useful without turning protected usage into a fixed ceiling.
Basic corner alignment was learned; one rookie-minicamp loss kept the assignment intact but lost physically at release. Coverage-lane work earned a teams role and he later served as outside reserve.
The recorded outside-reserve workload began after injuries elsewhere; individual technique evidence remains thin. Return credits are unreliable, and no dated retirement has been established.
Camp prepared him for safety rotation; coverage lanes held in preseason. Lowery/Rambo separated in communication, but regular-season defensive opportunity is unrecorded.

Previously taught special-teams jobs operated with less rescue through spring and strong multi-unit communication in camp. Defensive transition technique remains a baseline question, not a diagnosed flaw.
There is no recorded individual defensive or teams evaluation from the practice-squad year. His request for a teams assessment is a real follow-up, not evidence that he lacks value there.
Earlier NFL participation is part of his background; this staff's 2013 individual record is absent. Moving to the practice squad is not a measured regression.
Spring/camp and early-season specialist operation were recorded as clean. Later punt outcomes lack a complete split between instruction, kick and coverage; gross average is insufficient.
Clean early specialist operation provides a baseline; the late-season miss cluster and subsequent makes are review locators, not a diagnosis of technique or mentality.
Recorded spring/camp and Weeks 1–8 operation was clean. Later snaps lack their own assessment because the engine recorded no snapper credit; missing statistics are not missing contribution.

identity_basis: Frozen completed-2013-season syntheses copied from the exit-review baseline; never refreshed from later living profiles.
